html:
Somi Se'k is the homeland of the Esto'k Gna, the Carrizo and Comecrudo people of the lower Rio Grande valley in southern Texas and northern Tamaulipas. Esto'k Gna means "the people".

The Comecrudo and their neighbours were hunter-gatherers of the river valley and coastal plain, part of the many small groups the Spanish lumped together as Coahuiltecans and Tamaulipecos. Spanish missions and ranches in the 1700s and the new border of 1848 split and scattered them. The Comecrudo language was written down in 1886 from a few elderly speakers. Today the Carrizo/Comecrudo Tribe of Texas is not federally recognised. The Karankawa lived up the coast.
